questions.question_text: A rumour spreads through a town of $5000$ people at a rate proportional to the product of the number $x$ who have heard it and the number who have not. Which differential equation models this?

options.why: Added $x$ to the population instead of subtracting it, so the second factor is not the number who have not heard the rumour.
Left out the factor $x$, making the rate proportional only to the number who have not heard it.
Left out the factor $x$ and also added instead of subtracting.

questions.solution_text:
The number who have heard it is $x$.
The number who have not heard it is $5000-x$.
The rate is proportional to the product of these.
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=kx(5000-x)$

questions.question_text: A tank holds $200$ litres of brine containing $S$ kg of salt. Pure water flows in at $5$ litres per minute, and the well-mixed solution flows out at $5$ litres per minute. Which differential equation models $S$?

options.why: Used the flow rate as the constant, without dividing the salt by the volume of the tank.
Used the concentration $\frac{S}{200}$ but forgot to multiply it by the outflow of $5$ litres per minute.
Inverted the concentration, dividing the volume by the mass of salt.

questions.solution_text:
The concentration in the tank is $\dfrac{S}{200}$ kg per litre.
Salt leaves at $5\times\dfrac{S}{200}$ kg per minute, and none enters.
$\dfrac{dS}{dt}=-\dfrac{5S}{200}$
$=-\dfrac{S}{40}$

questions.question_text: A square metal sheet of side $x$ cm is heated, and its area increases at $0.6$ cm$^{2}$ per second. Find the rate at which the side length is increasing when $x=10$.

options.why: Differentiated $x^{2}$ as $x$ instead of $2x$, leaving out the factor of $2$.
Used $2x^{2}=200$ instead of $2x=20$ when applying the chain rule.
Divided by $0.1$ rather than by $20$, inverting the derivative.

questions.question_text: A population satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=aP-b$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants and $t$ is in years. The population stays constant at $5000$, and when $P=2000$ it is falling at $45$ per year. Find $a$.

options.why: Divided $45$ by $5000$, using the equilibrium population instead of the difference between the two populations.
Divided $45$ by $2000$, using only the second population and ignoring the equilibrium condition.
Divided $45$ by $1500$, taking the difference of the populations as $1500$ rather than $3000$.

questions.question_text: A herd is modelled by $\dfrac{dW}{dt}=0.05W-2$, where $W$ is the number of animals in hundreds and $t$ is in years. What does the term $-2$ represent?

options.text: $200$ animals are removed from the herd each year.
Two animals are removed from the herd each year.
options.why: Ignores the units: $W$ is measured in hundreds, so $2$ stands for $200$ animals.

options.text: The herd decreases by $2\%$ each year.
options.why: Reads a constant term as a percentage; a percentage decrease would be a multiple of $W$, not a constant.

options.text: The herd is $200$ animals below its carrying capacity.
options.why: Reads the constant as a population level; it is a rate, measured in hundreds of animals per year.

questions.solution_text:
$0.05W$ is the natural increase, $5\%$ of the herd each year.
$-2$ is a constant rate of removal, in hundreds of animals per year.
Since $W$ is in hundreds, $200$ animals are removed each year.

questions.question_text: The area of a drying puddle is modelled by $A=(5-0.2t)^{2}$ m$^{2}$, where $t$ is in hours. For which values of $t$ does the model make sense?

options.why: Ignores that $A$ starts increasing again once $5-0.2t$ becomes negative, which a drying puddle cannot do.
Used the $5$ inside the bracket as the time, rather than solving $5-0.2t=0$.
Divided $5$ by $0.1$ instead of by $0.2$ when solving for the time the puddle dries out.

questions.solution_text:
$A=0$ when $5-0.2t=0$.
$t=25$
For $t>25$ the bracket is negative and $A$ increases again, which cannot happen once the puddle has dried.
The model makes sense for $0\le t\le 25$.

questions.question_text: The mass $y$ grams of a product formed after $t$ minutes is modelled by $y=\dfrac{100t}{t+5}$. Which differential equation does $y$ satisfy?

options.why: Divided by $100$ rather than by $500$, so the constant does not match $\frac{500}{(t+5)^{2}}$.
Did not square $100-y$, which gives a rate proportional to $\frac{1}{t+5}$ instead of $\frac{1}{(t+5)^{2}}$.
Neither squared $100-y$ nor used the correct constant.

questions.question_text: A block of dry ice of mass $m$ kg satisfies $\dfrac{dm}{dt}=-0.6m^{\frac{2}{3}}$, where $t$ is in hours and $m(0)=64$. Find when half the original mass has gone, correct to one decimal place.

options.why: Assumed half the mass takes half the total melting time, but the rate slows as the block shrinks.
Gave the time for the block to disappear completely instead of the time to lose half its mass.
